source_meta._title: Order of rendering translucent block faces fails to update with camera position

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.7.2 in singleplayer, using keyboard and mouse, Creative mode, cheats enabled, no shaders or rendering-mod clients, and a render distance greater than the two-chunk minimum. The deterministic procedure uses the version-compatible 1.7.2 representation of the report's stained-glass Superflat preset.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact Java Edition version Minecraft 1.7.2; do not select the fix version 24w36a.
Use an unmodified client without OptiFine, Sodium, shaders, or other mods that can replace translucent-block rendering.
Make sure the computer has a working F3 key. On keyboards where F-keys control hardware functions, the Fn key may also need to be held.
Use a render distance above two chunks so that multiple stained-glass chunks around each teleport destination can render.
The test world must be newly generated from the supplied layer arrangement: bedrock, green stained glass, red stained glass, and blue stained glass, from bottom to top.
Do not press F3+T, change video settings, reload chunks, or intentionally move after the final teleport; those actions can alter the rendering state that the observation subsystem needs to inspect.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for the exact release 1.7.2, start it, and wait for the main menu. Do not use the 24w36a fix version.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is displayed and identifies the running version as Minecraft 1.7.2.

steps.action: From the main menu, open Options, then Video Settings. Set Render Distance to Normal or Far rather than Tiny, then return to the main menu. This ensures that more than two chunks are available around the teleport destinations.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is visible again and Render Distance is set above the minimum two-chunk setting.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open.

steps.action: Click the Game Mode button until it displays Game Mode: Creative. Creative mode is needed to perform the report's flying step without building anything.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen displays Game Mode: Creative.

steps.action: Select More World Options. Turn Allow Cheats ON so that both teleport commands can be run. Cycle World Type until Superflat is selected, and turn Generate Structures OFF to keep the glass plane unobstructed.
steps.success_cue: Allow Cheats is ON, World Type is Superflat, and Generate Structures is OFF.

steps.action: With Superflat selected, click Customize, then click Presets. Select all text in the preset text box, delete it, and enter the provided 1.7.2-compatible preset exactly. This is the historical numeric-ID equivalent of the report's named-ID preset: bedrock at the bottom, then green stained glass, red stained glass, and blue stained glass. In this syntax, 7 is bedrock, 95 is stained glass, and metadata 13, 14, and 11 select green, red, and blue respectively. Minecraft 1.7.2 requires the older preset format and does not have the report's the_void biome. ([ru.minecraft.wiki](https://ru.minecraft.wiki/w/%D0%A1%D1%83%D0%BF%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%BF%D0%BB%D0%BE%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D1%81%D1%82%D1%8C?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The preset text box contains exactly "2;7,95:13,95:14,95:11;1;" with no spaces or additional characters.

steps.action: Click Use Preset, then click Done to return to the main world-creation screen. Click Create New World.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft begins generating and loading the new world.

steps.action: Wait without issuing commands until world generation finishes, the surrounding terrain is rendered, and controls respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on an uninterrupted flat blue stained-glass surface; the red and green stained-glass layers are directly beneath it, and nearby chunks have finished rendering.

steps.action: Enter Creative flight by quickly pressing the Jump control twice; the default input is a double-tap of Space.
steps.success_cue: The player is flying and remains suspended instead of falling back onto the blue glass.

steps.action: Press F3 to display the debug overlay. Hold the Jump control, default Space, to ascend until the displayed Y coordinate is approximately 10 blocks above the glass surface. With this four-layer preset, a player initially stands at about Y=4, so a target near Y=14 is suitable. Release Space when that height is reached, then press F3 again to hide the overlay.
steps.exact_input: F3; hold Space until approximately Y=14; release Space; F3
steps.success_cue: The player is hovering approximately ten blocks above the blue stained-glass surface and is no longer ascending.

steps.action: Press T once to open the in-game chat input. The command must be executed in the player chat, not in the launcher or an external console.
steps.success_cue: The chat input line is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Type the report's first teleport command exactly, including the leading slash, then press Enter. The command moves the nearest player to X=100 and Z=100, preserves the current Y coordinate through the relative "~" argument, and sets camera yaw to 135 and pitch to 45.
steps.success_cue: The chat closes, the teleport completes, and the player is hovering near X=100 and Z=100 while looking in the command-specified direction.

steps.action: Do not continue immediately. Keep movement inputs released and wait until the stained-glass terrain around X=100, Z=100 has rendered across multiple chunks and the game responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Multiple surrounding stained-glass chunks are visible, loading activity has settled, and the client is responsive.

steps.action: Reload client resources using the report's debug shortcut: hold F3, tap T once while F3 remains held, then release both keys. On a keyboard with media-function F-keys, hold Fn as needed. F3+T reloads client resources, including textures and models. ([ja.minecraft.wiki](https://ja.minecraft.wiki/w/%E3%83%87%E3%83%90%E3%83%83%E3%82%B0%E7%94%BB%E9%9D%A2?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The client briefly pauses or redraws as resources reload, then returns to the world view.

steps.action: After the F3+T reload, keep all movement inputs released and wait until the surrounding stained-glass chunks have rendered again and the game responds normally. Do not move the camera or player during this wait unless required to restore game-window focus.
steps.success_cue: The player remains near X=100, Z=100 at the same height and orientation, multiple glass chunks are rendered, and the client is responsive.

steps.action: Press T once to reopen the in-game chat input.
steps.success_cue: The chat input line is open and ready for the second teleport command.

steps.action: Type the report's second teleport command exactly, including the leading slash, then press Enter. The command moves the nearest player to X=0 and Z=0, preserves the current Y coordinate, and sets yaw to -45 and pitch to 45. Executing this command is the reproduction trigger.
steps.success_cue: The chat closes and the player is teleported back near X=0 and Z=0 at the preserved height and command-specified camera orientation.

steps.action: Immediately release all movement and camera controls. Without pressing F3+T, changing video settings, or deliberately moving, wait only until the stained-glass terrain at the destination is rendered sufficiently for visual inspection. Hand control to the observation subsystem as soon as the destination view is available.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary near X=0 and Z=0, hovering above the glass at yaw -45 and pitch 45, and multiple destination chunks are available for inspection without any post-teleport movement or rendering reset.

stor.handoff_condition: The second teleport has just placed the stationary player near X=0 and Z=0 at the preserved flight height, with yaw -45 and pitch 45. Destination glass chunks are visible, and no movement, resource reload, chunk reload, or video-setting change has been performed after the teleport. Begin inspecting the translucent stained-glass layers now.
uncertainties: The report supplies the modern preset "minecraft:bedrock,minecraft:green_stained_glass,minecraft:red_stained_glass,minecraft:blue_stained_glass;minecraft:the_void", but the required first affected version, Minecraft 1.7.2, predates that named-ID preset format and predates the Void biome. The plan therefore uses the verified historical equivalent "2;7,95:13,95:14,95:11;1;", substituting the available plains biome while preserving the exact block layers and their order. ([ru.minecraft.wiki](https://ru.minecraft.wiki/w/%D0%A1%D1%83%D0%BF%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%BF%D0%BB%D0%BE%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D1%81%D1%82%D1%8C?utm_source=openai))
The report does not specify a world seed. No seed is selected because the custom Superflat layer arrangement is uniform and deterministic.

The report says to fly up approximately ten blocks and explicitly notes that the exact amount does not matter much. The target of approximately Y=14 assumes the player begins standing above the four generated layers near Y=4.

The report does not prescribe an exact render distance, but one report comment states that the issue could not be reproduced at a render distance of two chunks and could be reproduced above that setting. Normal or Far is selected as a deterministic practical setting for Minecraft 1.7.2.

The report's supplied reproduction was rewritten long after Minecraft 1.7.2. Although its layer arrangement can be translated to the older Superflat format, the report does not explicitly confirm the rewritten command sequence against the 1.7.2 user interface.
